question: Let \(P(n)\) and \(S(n)\) denote the product and the sum, respectively, of the digits of the integer \(n.\) For example, \(P(23)=6\) and \(S(23)=5.\) Suppose \(N\) is a two-digit number such that \(N=P(N)+S(N).\) What is the units digit of \(N?\)
solution:
Let \(a\) be the tens digit and \(b\) the units digit. Then \(1\le a\le9\), \(0\le b\le9\), and
\[
N=10a+b,\qquad P(N)=ab,\qquad S(N)=a+b.
\]
Substitute these expressions into the given condition:
\[
10a+b=ab+a+b.
\]
Subtracting \(a+b\) from both sides gives \(9a=ab\). Since a two-digit number has \(a\ne0\), division by \(a\) is valid and gives \(b=9\).

This digit works for every allowed \(a\), because \(9a+(a+9)=10a+9\). Thus the units digit is \(\boxed{9}\), choice E.
